history.dynasty: Built by the Oswal Jain community of Nagaur (no royal dynasty); one visitor account says built by a merchant in 1907

history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV seq 2152 duplicates the already-written records 2094.json ('glass-jain-temple-nagaur') and 892.json ('jain-glass-temple-nagaur') - all three describe the same Glass Jain Temple (Kanch Mandir) of Nagaur city, a small temple in the old-city bazaar lanes near Nagaur Fort (Achintagarh), famous for extensive coloured-glass and mirror mosaic work on walls, ceilings, pillars, doors and windows depicting Jain mythology. NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - it is a JAIN (Digambar) shrine; keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset. CSV town 'Nagaur' is correct for this record. Coordinates repeat 2094.json's Nagaur old-city pin; the geocoder matched 'Shri Digamber Jain Adinath Mandir' at the same point (verify).

name: Jain Glass Temple, Nagaur
town_description: Nagaur is one of Rajasthan's oldest cities - 'the cattle capital of India' - known for the Nagaur Fort (Ahhichatragarh), the Tarkeen Dargah and its January-February cattle fair.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport is the nearest airport (~250 km - per eIndiaTourism).
travel.railway: Nagaur Railway Station is ~3 km from the temple (per eIndiaTourism).
travel.road: Regular buses from Jaipur, Ajmer and Jodhpur; in the old-city bazaar area near Nagaur Fort - ask locals for the glass Jain temple lane.

visitor_information.opening_hours: 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM daily, no entry fee (per eIndiaTourism); remove shoes, dress modestly, no photography/videography inside (verify locally). Duplicate of 2094.json and 892.json: merge or remove.
